tldr: When machine output is cheap and everywhere, visible signs that a human cared become the scarcest and most valuable thing.
what: The idea that abundance moves scarcity. When anyone can generate a polished paragraph, polish proves nothing. Value shifts to what a machine cannot fake without a person choosing it: judgment, honesty about uncertainty, and taste for the right option for this reader.
why: Many people fear their work stops mattering once machines can make most of it. The essay argues the opposite: being visibly human becomes the differentiator, and it grows more valuable as it gets rarer.
how: It opens with a grandmother's coat, mended so often the mending became the coat, kept over flawless machine-made ones. Photography shows the pattern: once perfect images were free, the seeing mattered. A report someone clearly wrestled with earns trust. Use the tools for heavy hauling, then spend the freed attention on care.
takeaway: Be the visible stitches. Attention is finite and yours, and honest effort is the last thing that is genuinely yours to give.
